title: Extradural haematoma after head injury

related.why: trauma secondary survey (related clinical decisions, different task)

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee in the emergency department. A 24-year-old man was struck on the right side of his head during a football match. He briefly lost consciousness, seemed well, and now has a severe headache and repeated vomiting. A non-contrast CT head has been performed; the examiner will describe the image.
brief.task: Explain your assessment, interpretation and immediate plan. You are not asked to operate.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Recognise a time-critical expanding extradural bleed despite a deceptive early recovery.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Mistaking the lucid interval for reassuring recovery or waiting for a further fall in GCS before escalating.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Assess airway, breathing, circulation and disability now; obtain current GCS, pupils and observations, then request immediate senior and neurosurgical input.

flow: Assess ABCDE with cervical-spine precautions and repeat GCS/pupils.
Interpret the described CT and clinical pattern.
Identify impending deterioration and request neurosurgical review without delay.
Keep patient monitored, nil by mouth, obtain IV access and manage physiology with senior/anaesthetic support.
Communicate handover, prepare transfer and explain urgency to the relative.

grid.label: Immediate priorities
grid.fail: Reassures patient because he was initially alert; does not repeat ABCDE.
grid.borderline: Checks observations but does not prioritise airway or neurological trend.
grid.pass: Performs ABCDE and calls senior ED/trauma help, maintaining cervical precautions.
grid.high: Allocates simultaneous resuscitation and imaging review while anticipating airway decline.

grid.label: GCS and pupil trend
grid.fail: Does not reassess GCS or pupils after worsening vomiting.
grid.borderline: Mentions GCS but gives no serial plan or pupil examination.
grid.pass: States current GCS, pupillary size/reactivity and repeats documented observations.
grid.high: Specifies frequency, trend communication and immediate response to asymmetry or fall.

grid.label: CT interpretation
grid.fail: Calls a biconvex extra-axial collection a benign concussion.
grid.borderline: Identifies intracranial haemorrhage but cannot localise extradural anatomy.
grid.pass: Recognises a right biconvex/lens-shaped extradural collection and potential mass effect.
grid.high: Links temporal impact, middle meningeal injury and time-critical neurosurgical decision, avoiding invented size thresholds.

grid.label: Escalation
grid.fail: Plans discharge or routine outpatient neurosurgery.
grid.borderline: Requests a senior opinion only after prolonged observation.
grid.pass: Immediately contacts on-call neurosurgery and senior ED/trauma clinician.
grid.high: Uses concise SBAR including GCS trend, pupils, CT and transfer logistics.

grid.label: Resuscitation and airway
grid.fail: Leaves vomiting patient unattended and ignores worsening consciousness.
grid.borderline: Requests IV access but does not consider airway protection.
grid.pass: Maintains monitoring, IV access, analgesia/antiemetic and early anaesthetic assessment if consciousness falls.
grid.high: Explicitly aims to prevent hypoxia and hypotension, coordinating definitive airway if needed.

grid.label: Imaging and treatment pathway
grid.fail: Orders an outpatient repeat CT instead of acting on the current abnormality.
grid.borderline: Recognises abnormal scan but delays transfer pending another routine test.
grid.pass: Obtains urgent specialist interpretation and prepares for transfer or evacuation per neurosurgery.
grid.high: Plans prompt communication of CT findings and avoids needless delays to definitive treatment.

grid.label: Physiology and differentials
grid.fail: Attributes unequal pupils only to anxiety.
grid.borderline: Lists concussion without discussing intracranial pressure.
grid.pass: Explains evolving mass effect/herniation danger and checks anticoagulants/coagulopathy.
grid.high: Integrates bleeding risks and secondary brain injury prevention without distracting from evacuation.

grid.label: Handover and disposition
grid.fail: Proposes discharge with head-injury leaflet despite CT bleed.
grid.borderline: Says admit but names no accepting specialist.
grid.pass: Admits for monitored care and arranges neurosurgical transfer with documented observations.
grid.high: Provides explicit safety-focused handover, escort and repeat neurological observations during transfer.

grid.label: Communication
grid.fail: Tells family that a normal conversation rules out danger.
grid.borderline: States patient is unwell without explaining urgency.
grid.pass: Explains suspected brain bleed and urgent specialist assessment in clear terms.
grid.high: Checks understanding and explains why an earlier lucid interval cannot exclude deterioration.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: A young man has worsened after a head impact. What will you do first?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He was walking and talking earlier. I would take a routine history before examining him.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: He has vomited twice and is becoming sleepy. His GCS has fallen from 15 to 13; the right pupil is larger.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will check him again later if he continues to complain.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: CT shows a right biconvex extra-axial hyperdensity with local mass effect.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It may just be concussion. He had a lucid period.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will ask for a routine neurosurgical clinic review.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would book a repeat CT as an outpatient and act on that, not on this scan.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Why is the right pupil larger?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He is probably just anxious; that would explain it.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The nurse asks whether he can go home.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: If he feels better after an antiemetic, I could send him home with advice.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: His mother asks if this is dangerous.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It probably is not, because he spoke normally after the collision.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: This patient is increasingly drowsy after head trauma. Start.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I am the core surgical trainee. I will assess ABCDE immediately, protect his cervical spine until cleared, and request senior ED assistance.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Airway patent, SpO2 97% on air, BP 122/76, pulse 92.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I need the current and previous GCS, pupils and serial neurological observations.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: GCS was 15; it is now 13. Right pupil 5 mm sluggish, left 3 mm reactive.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That is deterioration with asymmetry. I will repeat and document findings and escalate now.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: He has vomited. Interpret his non-contrast CT: a right temporal biconvex hyperdense extra-axial collection with mass effect.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This is a right extradural haematoma, a neurosurgical emergency. The previous alert period does not reassure me.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Your next actions?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Contact the on-call neurosurgeon immediately with the CT and examination, and request senior trauma and anaesthetic support.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: He becomes harder to rouse.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will maintain oxygenation and blood pressure, reassess airway protection urgently with anaesthetics, establish IV access and continuous monitoring. I will not delay definitive care.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Can you wait for a repeat CT tomorrow?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No. The current abnormal scan and deterioration need urgent neurosurgical management; further imaging is for the treating specialists to decide.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Any risks to clarify?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will check anticoagulants, bleeding disorders and other injuries while resuscitation continues.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Where should he go?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Monitored care and urgent transfer to a neurosurgical unit if not onsite, with serial observations and a clear receiving-team handover.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: His mother asks what is happening.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The scan shows bleeding between the skull and brain covering. His condition can worsen rapidly, so specialists need to treat him urgently. I will update you as we act.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The patient was alert after impact but has become sleepy. Please lead the assessment.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will manage this as potentially evolving intracranial haemorrhage: ABCDE now, cervical protection, a senior trauma response and clearly assigned roles for observations, access and neurosurgical contact.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: SpO2 97%, BP 122/76, pulse 92, airway currently patent.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Please chart serial GCS by component and pupil size/reactivity every assessment. What has changed since arrival?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: GCS 15 to 13; right pupil 5 mm sluggish, left 3 mm brisk; he has vomited twice.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That trend is the critical signal. Please alert me immediately if either pupil or GCS changes again while I contact neurosurgery.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: CT is described as a right temporal biconvex extra-axial bleed with mass effect.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This is a right extradural haematoma. The temporal location fits possible middle meningeal vessel injury. I would not use the historical lucid interval to downgrade the urgency.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you refer?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: SBAR: 24-year-old head injury, new GCS drop to 13, unequal pupils, CT-confirmed right extradural bleed with mass effect. Please accept urgent neurosurgical transfer and advise definitive treatment; our team is stabilising him now.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: He is becoming less responsive.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Senior anaesthetic assessment immediately for airway protection. Meanwhile avoid hypoxia and hypotension, support ventilation and perfusion, monitor continuously, and keep him nil by mouth.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would an additional scan help?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will send the current images directly to the neurosurgical team. Repeat imaging must not delay urgent assessment and transfer if their decision is already time-critical.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: His medication list has not arrived.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Please urgently establish anticoagulant use and any coagulopathy and flag it in the referral, but do not hold escalation while retrieving history.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Transfer is arranged; what must accompany him?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Documented GCS components, pupils and trend; CT images/report; observations, treatments and a suitably trained escort with a clear deterioration plan.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: His mother says: “He was fine earlier. Why is this so serious?”

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That early improvement sometimes occurs before pressure from a bleed increases. He is now showing concerning changes. We are getting him specialist treatment urgently; I will update you at each step and answer your questions.

failures.move: Does not contact neurosurgery despite expanding extradural haemorrhage and falling GCS
Fails to protect airway/seek anaesthetics for progressive reduced consciousness
Discharges a patient with CT-confirmed extradural bleed
failures.consequence: risk of collapse outside monitored care.

failures.move: Ignores new anisocoria and GCS fall

recovery.when: If you assumed the lucid interval made this safe
recovery.line: I need to correct my earlier assumption: the lucid interval does not make this safe. With falling GCS and unequal pupils, I am calling neurosurgery now.

recovery.when: If you focused on the scan and not physiology
recovery.line: I have focused on the scan but must act on physiology too: I am reassessing ABCDE, airway protection and serial neurological observations immediately.

knowledge.fact: GCS and pupil changes guide serial deterioration assessment.
Urgent abnormal CT findings and clinical deterioration need appropriate neurosurgical discussion.
A new clinically important CT abnormality indicates admission, not routine discharge.

ABC stabilisation and prevention of secondary injury precede transfer, with suitably trained transfer staff; do not transfer someone with persistent hypotension despite resuscitation until the cause is found and they are stabilised.
The typical biconvex extradural imaging pattern and middle meningeal association are established clinical anatomy teaching; these are included as explanatory knowledge, not attributed to NG232 text.
The initial period of lucidity does not reliably exclude intracranial bleeding; used here as a scenario teaching concept, not a NICE guideline rule.

recall.think: Deterioration after a lucid period may be expanding extradural bleeding.
recall.say: Falling GCS, asymmetric pupils and CT bleed: urgent neurosurgery now.
do: ABCDE, serial neuro observations, senior/anaesthetic support, send CT and arrange safe transfer.

numbers.meaning: GCS trend and pupil change matter; no single bleed-size threshold is used in this station.

recall.trap: Do not discharge because the patient briefly appeared normal.
recall.finish: Document handover and tell the family why the urgency has changed.

sources.name: NICE. Head injury: assessment and early management. NG232
sources.supports: recommendations (sections 1.8, 1.9). Supports assessment, admission, monitoring and specialist transfer; not specific extradural image morphology.

partner.opening: Here is a patient who briefly recovered after a head injury and is now deteriorating.

reveals.trigger: Provide observations only on request or after candidate asks for ABCDE
reveals.finding: Airway patent, SpO2 97% on air, BP 122/76, pulse 92.

reveals.trigger: GCS/pupil deterioration follows the request for neurological trend (do not volunteer additional normal neurological findings)
reveals.finding: GCS was 15; it is now 13. Right pupil 5 mm sluggish, left 3 mm reactive.

reveals.trigger: CT description is supplied when asked to interpret the scan (examiner reads the CT description)
reveals.finding: a right temporal biconvex hyperdense extra-axial collection with mass effect.

curveballs.prompt: mother queries why previous improvement is irrelevant.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Checks understanding and explains why an earlier lucid interval cannot exclude deterioration.
